title: SOME/IP: Add configurable byte-array and UUID parameter types with improved tree display
description:
## Summary

This MR extends the SOME/IP payload dissector with two new configurable parameter types—**byte arrays** and **UUIDs**—and refines their tree presentation so values appear directly on the primary node without hidden child items.

## Changes

### New Parameter Types
- **Byte Array**: Configurable via UAT with optional length-of-length field (0/8/16/32 bits), custom names, and filter strings
- **UUID**: Configurable via UAT with optional length-of-length field, custom names, and GUID rendering

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 6fa3c750 - SOME/IP: Add configurable byte-array and UUID parameter types with improved tree display
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22357/diffs?diff_id=1569580039&start_sha=7cdbabc96c3928ff70a73a950aad3b4978533f38)

There's got to be a better way to configure this protocol/dissector than to continually add more UATs for each datatype that comes along.  Have you thought about an XML or other standard file format for configuration?  Wireshark doesn't need yet another "custom" file format to maintain in the dissector code, but a file format that already has a library for it would be fine.

added 1 commit
  • c44b7fd5 - SOME/IP: Add configurable byte-array and UUID parameter types with improved tree display
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22357/diffs?diff_id=1571415373&start_sha=6fa3c7505076541b29d0fd2e15cd0b4e8267e136)

There is no practical format for SOME/IP that would be suitable for this purpose. I have simply extended the existing configuration concept for SOME/IP in Wireshark, which is currently implemented. Anyone who doesn't want to use the feature doesn't need to touch the corresponding UATs. I think this is a pretty elegant solution.

  • d29d0864 - SOME/IP: Add byte-array and UUID parameter types with improved tree display
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22357/diffs?diff_id=1571485829&start_sha=c44b7fd5837af8502580831b6646576393df12ac)
@mmann78 Why are you rejecting the proposal? This proposal offers a significant improvement for the user.

Because I really don't like the UAT solution and I don't want it propagated further (also hoping to replace current UATs with a better solution). This isn't really what UATs were designed for.  I was hoping to get a better understanding of the protocol to make better suggestions.  Yes, there are a lot of different protocols that have "unique" features with niche user groups and Wireshark has many ways to handle them. But the code, "user experience", and maintenance should remain as consistent as possible.
Where can I find information on "setting up Wireshark to use SOME/IP"? (The fact that it's a question is a little troubling itself). There are numerous MRs for SOME/IP, but nothing jumps out as far as having a capture file with configured UATs to show successful dissection.

I don't think this useful extension should be rejected for a reason it can't control. If SOME/IP is currently configured with UATs, then UATs are the preferred method for such extensions.

Most SOME/IP configurations are very extensive and proprietary. They are typically generated automatically. I don't think anyone creates them manually, at most making minor modifications.

If there is to be a new format for configuring SOME/IP, that's a fundamental decision that isn't directly related to this valuable extension. I'm not a big fan of UATs myself. However, I assumed they weren't up for discussion. I would be the very first to welcome a new configuration format and would gladly make suggestions and contribute to its development. Personally, I would suggest a JSON format.

Therefore, my suggestion would be to first accept this proposal and then, as a second step, to consider the fundamental aspects of how SOME/IP should be configured in Wireshark.

P.S. The best way to understand SOME/IP's UATs is to look at their tooltips. These essentially replicate a table structure, similar to what you would find in a database.
Is there anything I can do to move this merge request forward?
